note: Community question bank for GCP Study Hub. Each question: id, cert, domain, question, options[], answer (index into options), explanation. Contributions welcome via PR.

questions.question: A streaming pipeline must group unbounded events into 5-minute buckets for aggregation. Which Dataflow concept do you use?
questions.explanation: Windowing (e.g., fixed 5-minute windows) groups unbounded streaming data into finite chunks so aggregations can be computed.

questions.question: Which BigQuery feature lets you query data stored in Cloud Storage without loading it into BigQuery-managed storage?
questions.explanation: External tables (and BigLake tables) let BigQuery query data in Cloud Storage in place, without ingesting it into native storage.

questions.question: You need event-time correctness in a stream where some events arrive late. What tracks progress of event time in Dataflow?
questions.explanation: Watermarks estimate how far event-time has progressed, letting the pipeline decide when a window is complete and how to handle late data.

questions.domain: Deploying and implementing a cloud solution
questions.question: You want a Cloud Run service to handle more concurrent requests per instance to reduce cost. Which setting do you change?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run concurrency controls how many simultaneous requests each container instance handles; higher concurrency can reduce the number of instances and cost.

questions.domain: Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution
questions.question: Which gcloud command interacts with a GKE cluster using kubectl?
questions.explanation: gcloud container clusters get-credentials fetches cluster credentials and configures kubectl to talk to the GKE cluster.

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: On the Professional Cloud Architect exam, how many case studies are presented to you?
questions.explanation: The exam guide publishes four case studies; the exam presents two of them (case-study questions are 20-30% of the exam). Study all four to be ready for whichever two appear.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud tool helps you set spending thresholds and receive alerts when costs approach them?
questions.explanation: Budgets and alerts in Cloud Billing let you define spending thresholds and get notified as actual or forecasted costs approach them.

questions.question: A regulator requires that encryption keys be stored in a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security module on Google Cloud. Which option meets this?
questions.explanation: Cloud HSM provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules for storing and using Cloud KMS keys.

questions.question: You need private, internal access to a published service (e.g., a SaaS or Google API) without traversing the public internet. Which feature provides this?
questions.explanation: Private Service Connect lets consumers access services (Google APIs, published services) privately using internal IPs, avoiding the public internet.

questions.question: You deployed a new Cloud Run revision and want to send only 5% of traffic to it initially. What enables this?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run lets you split traffic across revisions by percentage, so you can canary a new revision with a small slice of traffic.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud service stores built container images and other artifacts for deployment pipelines?
questions.explanation: Artifact Registry is the managed repository for container images, language packages, and OS packages used by CI/CD pipelines.

questions.question: For large-scale deep learning training that benefits from Google's custom accelerators, which hardware would you choose on Vertex AI?
questions.explanation: TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) are Google's custom accelerators optimized for large-scale deep learning training and inference.

questions.question: Which capability lets analysts train a simple ML model directly in BigQuery using SQL?
questions.explanation: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models using standard SQL inside BigQuery, without moving data or writing training code.

questions.question: An admin wants to apply a Gmail retention/compliance policy to only one department. What is the correct scoping mechanism?
options: An Organizational Unit (OU) or configuration group
questions.explanation: Workspace service settings and policies are scoped by Organizational Units (and configuration groups), enabling per-department configuration.

questions.domain: Designing scalable and highly available databases
questions.question: Which design choice helps avoid write hotspots in Spanner and Bigtable?
questions.explanation: Sequential/monotonic keys concentrate writes on one node/tablet (a hotspot). Well-distributed keys spread writes evenly across the system.

questions.question: You must load a one-time 5 TB CSV export from an on-prem system into BigQuery. Which approach is simplest and most cost-effective?
options: Stream rows via the Storage Write API
Upload to Cloud Storage, then batch-load into BigQuery
Insert rows with individual SQL statements
Use Memorystore as a staging layer
questions.explanation: For large one-time loads, stage files in Cloud Storage and run a batch load into BigQuery - batch loads are free and far cheaper than streaming for bulk data.

questions.question: A BigQuery query on a 2 TB table only needs the last 7 days of data by an event_date column. What reduces cost the most?
options: Partitioning the table by event_date and filtering on it
questions.explanation: Date partitioning lets BigQuery prune to only the relevant partitions, drastically reducing bytes scanned (and on-demand cost).

questions.question: Which service captures row-level changes from a source database and replicates them continuously for analytics?
questions.explanation: Datastream is a serverless change data capture (CDC) and replication service, often feeding BigQuery for near-real-time analytics.

questions.question: You need to restrict which columns of a BigQuery table an analyst group can see. What should you use?
questions.explanation: Column-level security uses policy tags (via Data Catalog/Dataplex) to control access to sensitive columns within a table.

questions.domain: Managing user accounts, domains, and directory
questions.question: Which tool synchronizes users and groups from an on-prem LDAP/Active Directory into Google Workspace?
questions.explanation: Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) provisions users and groups into Workspace/Cloud Identity from an existing LDAP or Active Directory.

questions.question: You want a specific department to have Google Drive external sharing disabled while the rest of the company keeps it. How?
options: Apply the setting to that department's Organizational Unit (OU)
questions.explanation: Settings applied at the OU level affect only users in that OU, enabling per-department policies like disabling external Drive sharing.

questions.question: Which feature lets admins require that only managed, compliant devices can access Workspace apps?
questions.explanation: Context-Aware Access enforces access policies based on user, device posture, and context (location, IP), allowing managed-device-only access.

questions.question: Where would an admin investigate a potential account compromise, review login events, and take bulk remediation actions?
questions.explanation: The security investigation tool (with the Alert Center) lets admins investigate logins and threats and perform bulk actions like resetting sessions.

questions.domain: Managing a solution for the enterprise
questions.question: Which Cloud SQL feature lets you recover the database to a specific moment in time after accidental data loss?
questions.explanation: Point-in-time recovery uses automated backups plus binary/transaction logs to restore to a specific timestamp.

questions.domain: Designing scalable and highly available databases
questions.question: A PostgreSQL-compatible database needs very high transactional throughput plus fast analytical queries on the same data. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: AlloyDB is PostgreSQL-compatible and adds a columnar engine for fast analytics alongside high transactional throughput (HTAP).

questions.question: To keep a Cloud SQL instance off the public internet while allowing app access from a VPC, you should:
options: Assign a public IP with open firewall
Use private IP / Private Service Connect
Expose it via a load balancer
questions.explanation: Configuring private IP (or Private Service Connect) keeps the instance on internal networking with no public exposure.

questions.question: You want to be alerted quickly when a service is burning its error budget abnormally fast. What should you configure?
options: A burn-rate alert on the SLO
questions.explanation: Error-budget burn-rate alerts fire when the budget is consumed faster than acceptable, catching both fast and slow failures tied to the SLO.

questions.question: Which practice manages infrastructure declaratively so environments are reproducible and version-controlled?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Config Controller) defines infrastructure declaratively for reproducible, reviewable, version-controlled environments.

questions.domain: Applying SRE principles to a service
questions.question: A team spends hours each week manually restarting a service. In SRE terms, this repetitive manual work is called:
questions.explanation: Toil is manual, repetitive, automatable operational work. Reducing toil through automation is a core SRE goal.

questions.question: An organization wants multiple projects to share a single central VPC managed by a network team. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Shared VPC lets a host project share its network with service projects, centralizing network administration while keeping project isolation.

questions.domain: Designing, planning, and prototyping a network
questions.question: GKE pods need their own IP ranges separate from node primary IPs. Which VPC feature provides this?
questions.explanation: VPC-native GKE clusters use alias IP (secondary) ranges on subnets to allocate pod and service IPs.

questions.domain: Managing, monitoring, and optimizing network operations
questions.question: Which tool helps you troubleshoot connectivity by testing reachability between two endpoints and showing the path?
options: Connectivity Tests in Network Intelligence Center
questions.explanation: Connectivity Tests (part of Network Intelligence Center) analyze configuration and simulate the path to diagnose reachability issues.

questions.question: A compliance rule requires you to control and manage the encryption keys used for data at rest. Which option satisfies this?
options: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS
questions.explanation: CMEK with Cloud KMS lets customers create, rotate, and control the keys protecting data at rest, meeting many compliance requirements.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud control enforces organization-wide guardrails such as blocking external IPs on VMs or disabling service account key creation?
questions.explanation: Organization policies set constraints that apply across the resource hierarchy, enforcing guardrails regardless of individual IAM grants.

questions.question: To grant employees access to internal web apps without a VPN, enforcing identity and context at the proxy, you use:
questions.explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy enforces per-request identity and context checks to protect applications, enabling secure access without a traditional VPN.

questions.question: A Cloud Run service must process messages reliably even during spikes, retrying failures. Which integration is best?
options: Pub/Sub push subscription with a dead-letter topic
Writing to Cloud Storage and polling
questions.explanation: A Pub/Sub subscription decouples producers from the Cloud Run consumer, provides retries, and a dead-letter topic captures messages that repeatedly fail.

questions.question: Which approach gives a Cloud Run service access to a database password without baking it into the image?
options: Store it in a public bucket
Pass it as a URL query param
questions.explanation: Secret Manager stores secrets securely; Cloud Run can mount them as environment variables or files at runtime with IAM-controlled access.

questions.question: A nightly job must score 50 million records where latency does not matter. Which prediction mode is most cost-effective?
questions.explanation: Batch prediction is designed for large, non-interactive scoring jobs and is far more cost-effective than keeping an online endpoint warm.

questions.question: Over time a deployed model's inputs drift from the training distribution, degrading accuracy. What detects this?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Model Monitoring tracks feature distributions to detect training/serving skew and drift and can trigger alerts for retraining.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate VMs to Google Cloud with minimal changes to the application. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Rehosting (lift and shift) moves workloads to the cloud with minimal changes, typically onto Compute Engine VMs.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud concept describes Google actively partnering with customers to improve their security posture, going beyond shared responsibility?
questions.explanation: Shared fate means Google takes an active role in helping customers be secure, offering secure defaults, blueprints, and guidance, rather than just drawing a responsibility line.

questions.domain: Innovating with data and Google Cloud
questions.question: A retailer wants to add image-based product search without training a model. Which option is fastest?
options: Train a custom model in Vertex AI
Use the pre-trained Cloud Vision API
Build a model in BigQuery ML
questions.explanation: Pre-trained AI APIs like Cloud Vision provide ready-made capabilities (label/object detection) with no model training required.

questions.domain: Introduction to digital transformation with Google Cloud
questions.question: Which fully managed productivity suite is an example of SaaS from Google?
questions.explanation: Google Workspace is Software as a Service - a fully managed application that users simply consume.

questions.domain: Deploying and implementing a cloud solution
questions.question: Which command deploys a container image to Cloud Run?
questions.explanation: gcloud run deploy deploys a container image as a Cloud Run service. kubectl is for Kubernetes; gcloud functions deploy is for Cloud Functions.

questions.question: You need to grant a group read-only access to all Cloud Storage buckets in a project. What is the best practice?
options: Grant each user the Owner basic role
Grant the group the predefined roles/storage.objectViewer at the project level
Download service account keys for each user
questions.explanation: Granting a predefined, least-privilege role (storage.objectViewer) to a Google group at the project level is the recommended approach.

questions.domain: Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution
questions.question: Which tool lets you view, filter, and export logs from Google Cloud resources?
questions.explanation: Cloud Logging stores, searches, and exports logs. Cloud Monitoring handles metrics and alerting; Trace and Profiler handle latency and performance.

questions.domain: Planning and configuring a cloud solution
questions.question: You want to connect two VPC networks privately so resources can communicate using internal IPs. Routing does NOT need to be transitive. What should you use?
questions.explanation: VPC Network Peering connects two VPCs for private internal-IP communication. It is non-transitive, which matches the requirement.

questions.domain: Setting up a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Where is billing linked in the Google Cloud resource hierarchy?
questions.explanation: A billing account is linked to projects. Each project is associated with exactly one billing account to pay for its resources.

questions.domain: Managing and provisioning a solution infrastructure
questions.question: A workload needs a highly available control plane for Kubernetes across multiple zones. What should you provision?
questions.explanation: A regional GKE cluster replicates the control plane across multiple zones in a region, providing high availability.

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: A business requires an RPO of near zero and an RTO of a few minutes for a critical database. Which strategy fits best?
options: A hot (active-active) multi-region deployment with synchronous replication
Cold standby in a single zone
questions.explanation: Near-zero RPO and minutes RTO require continuous replication and rapid failover - a hot/active or synchronously replicated multi-region setup (e.g., Spanner).

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: TerramEarth ingests huge volumes of telemetry from connected vehicles for later analytics. Which ingestion-to-analytics pipeline is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: High-volume streaming telemetry is ingested by Pub/Sub, processed by Dataflow, and landed in BigQuery for analytics - a canonical GCP pattern.

questions.question: Which service builds container images in a managed CI environment and stores them for deployment?
questions.explanation: Cloud Build runs the CI/build steps and Artifact Registry stores the resulting container images (and other artifacts).

questions.domain: Designing highly scalable, available, reliable apps
questions.question: An app needs an in-memory cache to reduce database load for frequently read data. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Memorystore provides managed Redis/Memcached for low-latency in-memory caching.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud Observability tool continuously analyzes CPU and memory consumption of production code with minimal overhead?
questions.explanation: Cloud Profiler continuously profiles CPU and memory usage of production applications with low overhead. Cloud Trace handles latency/distributed tracing.

questions.question: After an outage, your team writes a document focused on causes and improvements without assigning individual blame. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A blameless postmortem analyzes what happened and how to improve systems and processes, without blaming individuals - a core SRE practice.

questions.question: Which service protects web applications from DDoS attacks and common exploits at the edge, integrated with the global load balancer?
questions.explanation: Cloud Armor provides WAF rules and DDoS protection at the edge, integrated with the global external Application Load Balancer.

questions.question: You must centralize vulnerability findings, misconfigurations, and threat detections across your organization. Which service do you use?
questions.explanation: Security Command Center is the central security and risk management platform for posture, vulnerabilities, and threat findings across the organization.

questions.question: Which service provides managed DNS with public and private zones on Google Cloud?
questions.explanation: Cloud DNS is Google Cloud's scalable, managed authoritative DNS service, supporting both public and private zones.

questions.question: A company needs a dedicated 10 Gbps private physical connection to Google Cloud. Which product provides this?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct physical connection (10 or 100 Gbps) between on-premises and Google's network. Partner Interconnect is used when a direct connection is not feasible.

questions.question: To connect securely to a Cloud SQL instance over a private, encrypted channel without managing SSL certs manually, you should use:
options: A public IP with no restrictions
Direct root login over the internet
questions.explanation: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy provides secure, IAM-based connections to Cloud SQL without managing SSL certificates or allowlisting IPs.

questions.domain: Designing scalable and highly available databases
questions.question: Which database offers horizontal scalability with strong consistency and a 99.999% availability SLA for global relational workloads?
questions.explanation: Spanner uniquely combines horizontal scalability, strong consistency, and up to 99.999% availability for global relational workloads.

questions.question: You need sub-10ms lookups for a very large key-value/time-series dataset with high write throughput. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Bigtable delivers low-latency, high-throughput reads/writes for wide-column key/value and time-series data. BigQuery is for analytics, not low-latency lookups.

questions.question: A team wants to migrate existing on-prem Apache Spark jobs to Google Cloud with minimal changes. Which service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Dataproc runs managed Spark/Hadoop clusters, making it ideal for lifting-and-shifting existing Spark jobs. Dataflow would require rewriting to Apache Beam.

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: Which BigQuery techniques most directly reduce the amount of data scanned by date-filtered queries?
questions.explanation: Partitioning (e.g., by date) and clustering prune and co-locate data so queries scan less, reducing cost and improving performance.

questions.question: Which Vertex AI capability finds optimal hyperparameters automatically during training?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Vizier performs black-box optimization, including hyperparameter tuning, to improve model performance.

questions.question: A team with limited ML expertise wants to build a classification model from tabular data without writing training code. What should they use?
questions.explanation: AutoML on Vertex AI builds high-quality models from data with minimal code, ideal for teams with limited ML expertise.

questions.question: Which managed service orchestrates complex, scheduled data workflows using Apache Airflow?
questions.explanation: Cloud Composer is managed Apache Airflow for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring data pipeline workflows.

questions.question: Which service provides centralized data governance and cataloging across a data lake and warehouse on Google Cloud?
questions.explanation: Dataplex provides unified data governance, cataloging, and management across distributed data on Google Cloud.

questions.question: Which email authentication records help prevent spoofing and improve deliverability for a Workspace domain?
questions.explanation: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are the email authentication standards that reduce spoofing and improve deliverability.

questions.question: Which Workspace tool is used for legal holds, retention, and eDiscovery of user data?
questions.explanation: Google Vault manages retention, legal holds, and eDiscovery for Workspace data such as Gmail and Drive.

questions.question: A company wants to run containerized microservices without managing the underlying node infrastructure. Which Google Cloud product best fits?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run runs stateless containers serverlessly, scaling to zero with no node management. Compute Engine would require managing VMs.

questions.domain: Innovating with data and Google Cloud
questions.question: Which service is a serverless data warehouse for running SQL analytics over very large datasets?
questions.explanation: BigQuery is Google Cloud's serverless analytics data warehouse. Bigtable is operational NoSQL, Firestore is a document DB, and Cloud SQL is managed relational.

questions.question: Under Google Cloud's shared responsibility model, who is responsible for configuring IAM policies and securing customer data?
questions.explanation: Google secures the underlying infrastructure (security OF the cloud); the customer is responsible for IAM configuration and their data (security IN the cloud).

questions.domain: Introduction to digital transformation with Google Cloud
questions.question: Moving from buying servers upfront to paying only for cloud resources consumed is an example of shifting from:
questions.explanation: Cloud shifts spending from capital expenditure (buying hardware upfront) to operational expenditure (pay for what you use).

questions.domain: Innovating with data and Google Cloud
questions.question: A team needs to ingest a high-volume real-time stream of events for later processing. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Pub/Sub is a scalable messaging service for ingesting and distributing real-time event streams.

questions.question: An IAM policy granting Viewer is set at the folder level and Editor at the project level for the same user. What is the user's effective access on resources in that project?
options: The union: Editor (which includes Viewer-level read)
questions.explanation: IAM policies are inherited and additive. The effective policy is the union of all levels, so the user has Editor (which already includes read access).

questions.domain: Deploying and implementing a cloud solution
questions.question: Which resource provides autoscaling, autohealing, and rolling updates for a group of identical Compute Engine VMs?
questions.explanation: A Managed Instance Group uses an instance template and provides autoscaling, autohealing, and rolling updates. Unmanaged groups do not.

questions.domain: Planning and configuring a cloud solution
questions.question: In Google Cloud networking, what is the scope of a VPC network and of a subnet?
options: VPC is zonal; subnet is regional
VPC is global; subnet is regional
VPC is regional; subnet is zonal
questions.explanation: A VPC network is a global resource, while subnets are regional and span all zones in their region.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to give a Compute Engine VM permission to call Google Cloud APIs?
options: Embed a user's password in the VM
Download a service account JSON key onto the VM
Attach a service account to the VM
questions.explanation: Attaching a service account to the VM is preferred. Downloading JSON keys is discouraged because keys are long-lived secrets that can leak.

questions.domain: Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution
questions.question: Which command sets the active project for subsequent gcloud commands?
questions.explanation: gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID sets the active project in the current configuration.

questions.domain: Planning and configuring a cloud solution
questions.question: A private VM with no external IP needs outbound internet access to download OS updates. What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for instances without external IP addresses, without exposing them to inbound connections.

questions.domain: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
questions.question: An application requires a relational database that is globally distributed with strong consistency and 99.999% availability. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Spanner provides globally distributed, strongly consistent relational data with up to 99.999% availability in multi-region configurations. Cloud SQL is regional.

questions.question: To prevent data exfiltration from BigQuery and Cloud Storage to resources outside a trusted boundary, you should implement:
questions.explanation: VPC Service Controls create a security perimeter around managed services like BigQuery and Cloud Storage to mitigate data exfiltration.

questions.question: In SRE terms, what does an error budget represent?
options: The money allocated to fixing bugs
The allowed amount of unreliability, equal to 1 minus the SLO
The number of engineers on call
questions.explanation: The error budget is the acceptable level of unreliability, calculated as 1 minus the SLO. It governs how much risk a team can take with releases.

questions.domain: Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes
questions.question: A steady, predictable batch workload runs 24/7 on Compute Engine. Which pricing approach minimizes cost while guaranteeing capacity?
questions.explanation: Committed use discounts offer significant savings for steady, predictable workloads while guaranteeing capacity. Spot VMs are cheaper but can be preempted.

questions.question: To decouple a web frontend from backend processing with at-least-once delivery and fan-out to multiple subscribers, you should use:
questions.explanation: Pub/Sub provides many-to-many, at-least-once messaging with fan-out to multiple subscribers. Cloud Tasks is for explicit, rate-limited task dispatch to a single worker.

questions.question: You want to roll out a new Cloud Run revision to 10% of traffic before full release. What feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run supports traffic splitting across revisions, enabling canary deployments by sending a percentage of traffic to a new revision.

questions.question: Which service should store database passwords and API keys for an application?
questions.explanation: Secret Manager securely stores and version-controls secrets like passwords and API keys, with IAM-based access and audit logging.

questions.question: Which pair correctly describes an SLI and an SLO?
options: SLI is a legal contract; SLO is a measurement
SLI is a measured indicator; SLO is a target for that indicator
SLO is a measured indicator; SLI is a penalty
questions.explanation: An SLI (Service Level Indicator) is a measured value such as latency or error rate; an SLO (Service Level Objective) is the target for that SLI.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud service provides managed progressive delivery (e.g., canary) to GKE and Cloud Run?
questions.explanation: Cloud Deploy is a managed continuous delivery service that orchestrates progressive rollouts to targets like GKE and Cloud Run. Cloud Build handles the CI/build step.

questions.question: What is the most secure way for an on-prem or external workload to authenticate to Google Cloud without long-lived keys?
options: Download a service account JSON key
questions.explanation: Workload Identity Federation lets external identities impersonate service accounts using short-lived credentials, avoiding long-lived JSON keys.

questions.question: Which service discovers, classifies, and de-identifies sensitive data such as PII?
questions.explanation: Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) discovers, classifies, and de-identifies or tokenizes sensitive data like PII.

questions.question: You need a globally scoped Layer 7 load balancer with Cloud CDN for a web application. Which do you choose?
questions.explanation: The global external Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7, is global, and integrates with Cloud CDN - ideal for global web apps.

questions.question: Which option provides a highly available VPN connection to Google Cloud with a 99.99% SLA?
questions.explanation: HA VPN provides a 99.99% availability SLA using redundant tunnels and interfaces. Classic VPN offers a lower SLA.

questions.domain: Designing scalable and highly available databases
questions.question: An IoT platform ingests millions of time-series writes per second with single-digit millisecond reads. Which database fits best?
questions.explanation: Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database designed for very high throughput and low-latency reads/writes, ideal for time-series and IoT workloads.

questions.question: Which service performs minimal-downtime database migrations into Cloud SQL or AlloyDB with continuous replication?
questions.explanation: Database Migration Service (DMS) performs homogeneous and heterogeneous database migrations with continuous replication for minimal downtime.

questions.question: Which service runs unified batch and streaming data pipelines serverlessly using Apache Beam?
questions.explanation: Dataflow is the serverless Apache Beam runner for unified batch and streaming pipelines. Dataproc runs managed Spark/Hadoop clusters.

questions.domain: Preparing and using data for analysis
questions.question: To reduce the cost of on-demand BigQuery queries that filter by date, you should:
options: Store data as CSV in Cloud Storage
Partition the table by date and cluster by common filter columns
questions.explanation: Partitioning by date and clustering by frequently filtered columns reduces the bytes scanned, directly lowering on-demand query cost.

questions.question: Which service provides managed Apache Airflow for orchestrating data pipelines?
questions.explanation: Cloud Composer is managed Apache Airflow, used to author, schedule, and monitor complex data pipeline workflows.

questions.question: An application needs low-latency, real-time predictions from a trained model. Which Vertex AI capability should you use?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI online prediction deploys a model to an endpoint for low-latency, real-time inference. Batch prediction is for large, non-interactive jobs.

questions.question: Which Vertex AI feature helps detect training/serving skew and feature drift in production models?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Model Monitoring tracks input feature distributions to detect training/serving skew and drift, alerting when models degrade.

questions.domain: Collaborating to manage data and models
questions.question: What is the purpose of Vertex AI Feature Store?
options: To centrally manage and serve ML features for reuse and consistency
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Feature Store centralizes feature management and serving, promoting reuse and reducing training/serving skew.

questions.question: Which tool is best for building interactive dashboards on top of BigQuery for business users?
questions.explanation: Looker Studio (and Looker) create interactive dashboards and reports, commonly connected to BigQuery for self-serve BI.

questions.question: A low-code, visual way to build ETL pipelines on Google Cloud is provided by:
questions.explanation: Cloud Data Fusion is a fully managed, visual (low-code) data integration service for building ETL/ELT pipelines.

questions.question: Which Workspace feature enforces access decisions based on device and context (such as IP or device security status)?
questions.explanation: Context-Aware Access applies granular access controls to Workspace apps based on user identity, device posture, and context like IP location.

questions.domain: Managing user accounts, domains, and directory
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Organizational Units (OUs) in Google Workspace?
options: To apply settings and service policies hierarchically to groups of users
questions.explanation: OUs let administrators apply settings and control service access hierarchically to subsets of users within the organization.
